planDigest.mismatchBehavior: Stop before executing any task and regenerate this sidecar from the rewritten plan.

scope: One foundation plan with four execution phases, three blocking go/no-go gates, and D8 final acceptance.

tasks.subject: Establish Python 3.12 project metadata and the canonical lock
tasks.observableResult: A Hatchling src/ project pinned by .python-version syncs reproducibly from uv.lock, exports the launcher's hashed requirements from that lock, and imports as an installed package without path manipulation.
commands: uv run python -c "import sys; assert sys.version_info[:2] == (3, 12)"
tasks.expectedResult: Every command exits 0; .python-version is 3.12; the export has no diff after regeneration; Python reports 3.12; import scoutmb resolves from the editable installed package.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: If selection, resolution, or export is not reproducible, correct project markers and regenerate uv.lock; never hand-edit .python-version, the lock, or exported pins to fake parity.

tasks.subject: Add green quality, lock, and capability-environment CI
tasks.observableResult: Every pull request runs green lint, format, type, lock, branch-coverage, and explicit core/acquisition/PDF/all-extras environment checks on Python 3.12.
tasks.expectedResult: All commands exit 0; the workflow pins Python 3.12; core, acquisition, PDF, and all-extras jobs name their sync command; no unexpected skip or live-service smoke passes silently.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Narrow documented mypy exceptions only around legacy or untyped third-party adapters. Repair an unavailable capability environment rather than skipping it or weakening strict settings.

tasks.subject: Establish supply-chain and supported-platform evidence
tasks.observableResult: Phase A CI produces a reproducible locked-dependency vulnerability result, license decision, development SBOM, clean-build metadata, and an explicit supported-platform file.
commands: uv run python tools/build_dependency_evidence.py --lock uv.lock --output build/evidence/phase-a
tasks.expectedResult: All commands exit 0; no unexpired unapproved finding remains; the SBOM and metadata reference the exact lock; platform metadata distinguishes supported, best-effort, and unsupported.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep production behavior unmoved, correct the lock/policy/metadata, regenerate all evidence together, and do not waive an unknown license, vulnerability, or platform assumption.

tasks.subject: Enforce offline-by-default tests and application egress policy
tasks.observableResult: Any default-test attempt to reach a non-loopback address, including from Playwright redirects, frames, popups, workers, service workers, WebSockets, alternate ports, direct IPs, or browser subprocesses, fails before private data leaves the process.
tasks.expectedResult: Both commands exit 0; sentinels record zero non-loopback requests; every hostile browser surface fails with ExternalNetworkBlocked; the real-service request count remains zero.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Disable the new network adapter, retain the local fake path, and repair the missing guard. Never recover by allowlisting the real host in default tests.

tasks.subject: Create synthetic factories and a repository privacy tripwire
tasks.observableResult: Deterministic committed factories cover identity, token, requirement, payload, UI, installer, migration, and output edge cases and fail closed if likely private data is introduced.
tasks.expectedResult: Both commands exit 0; the scanner prints private-data findings: 0 without echoing matched source text; every Gate 1 matrix category can name a synthetic fixture.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Quarantine the new fixture outside the repository, improve the factory or scanner, and rerun. Do not add real values to an allowlist.

tasks.subject: Add optional private-corpus verification
tasks.observableResult: pytest --corpus-dir raw_data always runs the synthetic suite and, when the local corpus exists and matches its manifest lock, adds redacted read-only private-corpus checks.
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0 with synthetic tests always executed and either private corpus: PASS or private corpus: SKIPPED (not present); output contains no names, IDs, tokens, paths, or URLs.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Stop at manifest or redaction failure, remove only tool-owned derived staging, preserve raw_data/ untouched, and require explicit manifest review before rerunning.

tasks.subject: Characterize every input and PDF extraction contract
tasks.observableResult: A table-driven suite pins XLSX, CSV, JSON, text, directory/glob expansion, field aliases, deduplication, QR variants, the exact seven attendee columns, ordering, strict mode, corrupt/stale-error behavior, and optional-capability absence.
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0; every locked matrix row names its fixture and observable; the PDF environment executes real adapter imports and the core-only path remains separately testable.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Correct mistaken expectations from observed legacy output. Do not alter production parsing or mark a capability test skipped to make the matrix green.

tasks.subject: Characterize ScoutingEvent and browser-session behavior against a local fake
tasks.observableResult: A loopback fake and real Playwright API surface reproduce session setup, payload shapes, redirects, schema drift, retryable/terminal errors, deduplication, and request counts without contacting the real service.
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0; fake request counts match; external-request sentinels remain zero; schema variants are named fixtures; unexpected Playwright API use fails rather than being accepted.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Extend the local fake with the missing observed shape. Never capture a new live response in an automated test or weaken the egress policy.

tasks.subject: Characterize inference, artifacts, interfaces, and baseline performance
tasks.observableResult: The remaining legacy matrix pins requirement parsing, inference and both consumers, non-mutation, output schemas, CLI/UI defaults, errors, request counts, startup, runtime, memory, installed footprint, and artifact sizes using repeated samples.
commands: uv run python tools/measure_baseline.py --corpus synthetic --repetitions 5 --output build/baseline.json
tasks.expectedResult: Tests exit 0; build/baseline.json records machine class, corpus revision, five samples, request counts, memory, sizes, installed footprint, variance, and no placeholders.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep wall time non-blocking, fix missing observables, and rerun on the same machine class. Do not move code while a correctness row is absent or red.

tasks.subject: Characterize bootstrap, local web, run lifecycle, and static UI behavior
tasks.observableResult: Every remaining Gate 1 row for installer/bootstrap, local web security, lifecycle, and user-visible progress/quiet/error behavior is tied to a legacy test and classified as preserve, intentional-change, or new-acceptance.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; every Gate 1 category and graph-identified bootstrap/UI flow has an observable, fixture, test, and disposition; known deficiencies cannot silently become final parity.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Restore a mistaken expectation from observed legacy output, keep unsafe legacy paths constrained to loopback/throwaway roots, and block Gate 1 until every row has a reviewed disposition.

tasks.subject: Characterization go/no-go
tasks.observableResult: Phase A produces one reproducible offline characterization, privacy, supply-chain, platform, and performance evidence set with a recorded GO; any missing row or failing command records NO-GO and blocks Phase B.
commands: uv run python tools/build_dependency_evidence.py --lock uv.lock --output build/evidence/phase-a
uv run python tools/check_private_data.py tests build/baseline.json build/evidence/phase-a
tasks.expectedResult: All commands exit 0; every matrix row is classified and tested; no non-loopback request, unexpected skip, unapproved supply-chain finding, ambiguous platform assumption, coverage regression, or private-data finding occurs; locks, exports, SBOMs, and baselines are reproducible.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Stop. Assign the failing evidence to A1-A10, preserve legacy production behavior, regenerate related evidence together, and rerun the entire gate. Waivers do not open it.

tasks.subject: Introduce package boundaries and compatibility entry points
tasks.observableResult: scoutmb introduces only the needed core, features, ports, adapters, interfaces, runtime, and resources modules; legacy top-level scripts delegate to package entry points; no first-party code mutates sys.path.
tasks.expectedResult: All commands exit 0; both help outputs retain the characterized contract; imports work from an installed package without repository-root assumptions.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep the compatibility wrapper as the active path, move one symbol group back, and restore parity. Do not add a path mutation or duplicate logic in the wrapper.

tasks.subject: Establish typed core, clocks, errors, configuration, and DTO versions
tasks.observableResult: Pure immutable models represent attendees, classes, requirements, runs, artifact generations, typed errors, versioned DTOs, UTC wall time, and monotonic deadlines.
commands: uv run pytest tests/unit/core tests/unit/test_clocks.py tests/contracts/test_dto_versions.py -q
uv run mypy --strict src/scoutmb/core src/scoutmb/features src/scoutmb/ports src/scoutmb/runtime
tasks.expectedResult: Both commands exit 0; core tests require no filesystem, network, browser, UI, or system clock.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Remove the incomplete DTO from interface composition, keep boundary dictionaries behind the legacy adapter, and repair typed construction without weakening strict checks.

tasks.subject: Move input and PDF work behind ports with parity
tasks.observableResult: Input loading and PDF extraction are adapter implementations selected by feature services; core-only installation can load non-PDF inputs without importing PDF/OpenCV dependencies.
commands: uv run pytest tests/parity/test_input_adapter_parity.py tests/parity/test_pdf_adapter_parity.py tests/packaging/test_core_imports.py -q
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; legacy and new DTO projections match for every A7 fixture; core-only import succeeds with optional libraries absent.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Select the legacy adapter at the interface composition root and fix one mismatch at a time. Do not make PDF/OpenCV core dependencies.

tasks.subject: Implement the ScoutingEvent session gateway and schema-drift boundary
tasks.observableResult: One adapter owns the attendee session, URL allowlist, payload validation, schema profiles, redaction, and drift diagnostics while feature code sees only typed port DTOs.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; local fake profiles and normalized legacy/new results match; drift cases return typed errors; diagnostics contain no cookies, tokens, upstream IDs, or raw bodies.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep the legacy local-fake adapter selected, store only redacted drift metadata, and add a reviewed schema profile. Never fall back to permissive parsing.

tasks.subject: Add bounded acquisition retries, deadlines, checkpoints, and a circuit breaker
tasks.observableResult: The acquisition service bounds attempts and elapsed time, deduplicates requests, checkpoints resumable progress, stops on terminal schema/auth errors, and closes all attendee-session resources.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; fake request ledger proves bounded counts/no duplicates; resource tracker ends at zero; every normalized legacy/new difference is in the reviewed change manifest.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Disable the new acquisition service at interface composition, retain its checkpoint for diagnosis, and restore the characterized adapter. Do not increase budgets to mask leaks.

tasks.subject: Replace name identity with fail-closed upstream IDs and per-run UUIDv4
tasks.observableResult: Two same-named attendees remain distinct through acquisition, inference, resume, and reports; blank/malformed upstream IDs stop the attendee before work; shareable IDs are full UUIDv4 values unique within each run.
commands: uv run pytest tests/unit/core/test_identity.py tests/integration/test_identity_flow.py tests/parity/test_intentional_changes.py -q
tasks.expectedResult: Both commands exit 0; UUID version is 4; two runs use unlinkable UUIDs; privacy scan reports zero upstream IDs/tokens; the A9 known-defect expectation is replaced by one reviewed intentional difference and the correct contract.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Fail the affected run before publication, preserve redacted diagnostic state, and restore the legacy adapter only for local fake comparison. Never synthesize identity from a name.

tasks.subject: Version schemas/templates and publish each artifact atomically
tasks.observableResult: CSV, JSON, HTML, and email templates have explicit contract versions; single-artifact writes use same-directory temporary files, flush/fsync where required, atomic replace, and cleanup while preserving the prior file on failure.
commands: uv run pytest tests/contracts/test_artifact_schemas.py tests/contracts/test_report_template.py tests/unit/files/test_atomic_file.py tests/parity/test_output_parity.py tests/privacy/test_artifacts.py -q
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; goldens and normalized parity match; template edge cases round-trip; injected render/write/flush/file-fsync/close/replace/directory-fsync failures preserve old bytes or return the documented post-replace indeterminate-durability result without a second overwrite.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep the previous schema version active, retain failed output only in private staging, and fix the writer. Do not partially overwrite the published artifact.

tasks.subject: Publish multi-file report generations atomically
tasks.observableResult: A complete report/email set is staged under a generation ID, validated, then activated by one atomic manifest pointer; readers see the prior or new generation, never a mixture.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0 across every artifact/manifest/pointer failure; the active pointer names one complete generation; every malformed/future/escaping/hash-mismatched consumer input fails closed.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Leave the previous manifest active, quarantine the incomplete staging directory, and offer explicit retry/inspection. Never repair by merging directories.

tasks.subject: Introduce durable run state and lifespan-owned job supervision
tasks.observableResult: Legal run transitions, checkpoints, pause/resume/cancel, startup recovery, bounded workers/queue, and graceful shutdown are owned by one supervisor rather than ad hoc threads or module globals.
commands: uv run pytest tests/unit/jobs/test_run_state.py tests/integration/test_job_supervisor.py tests/parity/test_operation_parity.py -q
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; no non-daemon worker or resource survives each test; restart produces the documented terminal/resumable outcome.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Stop accepting new jobs, persist current checkpoint, cancel owned children within the grace period, and keep the legacy operation adapter selectable until lifecycle tests pass.

tasks.subject: Secure the loopback web boundary and stream uploads safely
tasks.observableResult: A lifespan-created application uses a random session secret, loopback-only binding, Host/Origin validation, authentication, CSRF protection, CSP, containment-safe paths, streaming upload limits, parser budgets, and redacted errors.
commands: uv run pytest tests/security tests/integration/test_app_lifespan.py tests/parity/test_local_web_parity.py -q
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; unauthorized/cross-origin/oversized/traversal cases are rejected; memory remains within the upload budget; valid loopback flows retain characterized responses.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep the prior UI disabled outside loopback, preserve completed runs, and repair the security boundary. Do not bypass authentication for desktop convenience.

tasks.subject: Compose CLI, web, and desktop entry points with port-zero rendezvous
tasks.observableResult: CLI, local web, and desktop launch the same feature services; the server binds port 0 and reports the actual authenticated rendezvous, eliminating bind-close-rebind races.
tasks.expectedResult: Both commands exit 0; parallel launches receive distinct OS-assigned ports; doctor reports no live network use and no path/import mutation.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Abort the attempted launch without killing an unrelated process, keep the existing instance/rendezvous intact, and restore the prior entry adapter while fixing composition.

tasks.subject: Prove clean package and copied-release startup
tasks.observableResult: Wheel and sdist install in clean environments; the launcher copies or installs src/scoutmb, package data, and compatibility entry points into a clean release root that starts without the repository present.
commands: uv run python tools/rebuild_wheel_from_sdist.py --dist dist --output build/from-sdist
tasks.expectedResult: All commands exit 0; both archives contain required package data and exclude raw_data/, private fixtures, tests, logs, tokens, and secrets; the original wheel and wheel rebuilt from sdist pass clean smoke tests with repository paths hidden/unmounted.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep the previously working source-copy manifest, correct package-data/build rules, rebuild from clean state, and do not add runtime fallbacks to repository files.

tasks.subject: Identity, output, and runtime go/no-go
tasks.observableResult: Phase B has a complete parity/privacy/failure-injection run and a recorded GO; any identity ambiguity, mixed output generation, leaked resource, insecure route, or clean install failure records NO-GO and blocks Phase C.
commands: uv run pytest tests/architecture tests/compat tests/parity tests/contracts tests/privacy tests/security tests/integration tests/packaging -m "not live_service" -q
uv run python tools/check_private_data.py build/test-artifacts dist
tasks.expectedResult: All commands exit 0; same-name attendees stay separate; missing identity fails closed; previous outputs survive injected failures; no sensitive value, leaked resource, unauthorized route, path mutation, or repository dependency remains.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Stop. Restore the relevant compatibility adapter as default, preserve failed generations privately, and return the defect to its B task. Waivers do not open the gate.

tasks.subject: Resolve and manage supported installed-data roots
tasks.observableResult: The application proves a supported local data root, applies current-user permissions, exposes category sizes/retention/deletion, and safely backs up, restores, and prunes each locked retention class.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; supported local roots pass capability and permission probes; unsupported active roots fail before mutation; UI/CLI report the same categories; dry-run, deletion, backup, and restore preserve every protected reference byte-for-byte.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Stop cleanup/activation, retain the backup and active root, quarantine invalid restore staging, and require explicit operator retry after diagnostics.

tasks.subject: Add OS-backed ownership, single-instance rendezvous, and activation
tasks.observableResult: Exactly one launcher owns the installation; a second launch authenticates to the live rendezvous, requests foreground activation, and exits without starting another app.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0 across repeated multi-process matrices; one owner starts; activation, OS-denied focus, and stale rendezvous return their documented outcomes; an unresponsive owner or mutating CLI returns stable busy/unresponsive; no duplicate app starts or unrelated process is signaled.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: If ownership cannot be proven, do not launch or break the lock automatically. Show recovery guidance and preserve the lock/rendezvous evidence for diagnosis.

tasks.subject: Implement copy-only SHA-256 migration and activation marker
tasks.observableResult: A throwaway legacy root is inventoried, copied into staging, collision-safe, SHA-256 verified, then activated with a versioned marker; interruption resumes safely and original files remain untouched.
commands: uv run scoutmb migrate --source build/legacy-root --destination build/new-root --dry-run
tasks.expectedResult: Both commands exit 0; dry-run manifest is deterministic; source hashes are unchanged; staging/promotion/marker boundaries survive injection; activation and old-root markers reference the complete verified inventory and production mode cannot start without backup evidence.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Leave source and current active destination untouched, retain staging/manifest, and resume from the last verified item. Never delete a collision or write a success marker early.

tasks.subject: Detect split-brain writes on every launch and preserve recovery snapshots
tasks.observableResult: Every launch while the legacy root exists detects writes before, during, or after cutover; changed state is snapshotted with hashes/provenance and mutation pauses for explicit operator reconciliation.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; each divergent write creates a bounded redacted diagnostic and content-complete protected snapshots; active data is not silently changed.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Freeze cleanup and affected publication, keep both snapshots indefinitely, and require explicit reconciliation. Rescan hashes before resuming.

tasks.subject: Version durable state and enforce the activation compatibility tuple
tasks.observableResult: Runs, checkpoints, settings, release metadata, and activation pointer carry schema versions; an activation tuple proves executable, state generation, capability set, and protocol compatibility before startup.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; incompatible tuples never launch; failed conversions preserve the old state generation and executable pointer.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Reactivate the last-known-good tuple atomically and retain failed staged state as a protected recovery snapshot. Do not downgrade state in place.

tasks.subject: Harden downloads, archives, disk budgets, and capability cache ownership
tasks.observableResult: Downloads are streamed to staging, size/hash/content validated, archives reject traversal/link/device/expansion attacks, disk reserves are checked before writes, and cache eviction respects active/rollback capability references.
commands: uv run pytest tests/launcher/test_downloader.py tests/security/test_safe_extract.py tests/launcher/test_disk_budget.py tests/launcher/test_capability_cache.py -q
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0; hostile/oversized/mismatched inputs fail before activation; injected disk exhaustion leaves current install/cache valid and staging recoverable or cleaned.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Delete only verified unreferenced staging through the cache service, keep current and rollback payloads, and offer retry after sufficient disk/network availability.

tasks.subject: Install releases transactionally with readiness proof and rollback
tasks.observableResult: A release installs into a versioned staging directory, validates package and state compatibility, launches with a one-time readiness nonce, then atomically switches current.json; any failure returns executable and state to the last-known-good tuple.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0 for success and injected failures; pointer is always old or new valid JSON; after rollback the prior app starts and reads the restored state generation offline.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Atomically restore the last-known-good pointer and state generation, retain failed release diagnostics/staging within budget, and never mutate the working release in place.

tasks.subject: Migration and release go/no-go
tasks.observableResult: A throwaway copy of the live layout completes migrate, N-to-N+1 update, forced rollback, and N restart with a recorded GO; any source mutation, ownership ambiguity, corruption, split-brain loss, or rollback incompatibility records NO-GO and blocks Phase D.
commands: uv run pytest tests/storage tests/migration tests/launcher tests/contracts/test_state_compatibility.py tests/integration/test_backup_restore.py tests/integration/test_activation_tuple.py -q
uv run python tools/rehearse_upgrade.py --legacy-root build/gate3/legacy --work-root build/gate3/work --sequence N,N+1,N --require-backup-receipt build/gate3/backup.json
tasks.expectedResult: All commands exit 0; source hashes remain unchanged; simultaneous launchers have one owner; collisions and split-brain data are preserved; disk-full/interruption cannot corrupt active data; N restarts offline after rollback; reports are redacted.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Stop. Preserve the throwaway evidence and recovery snapshots, reactivate N, and return the failure to its C task. Do not run migration against the live installation.

tasks.subject: Split core, acquisition, browser, and PDF capability payloads
tasks.observableResult: Core, ScoutingEvent acquisition, managed Chromium, and PDF/OpenCV payloads have separate manifests, dependency closures, cache identities, compatibility ranges, install states, and reference-counted removal rules; core imports with every optional payload absent.
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0; manifests/hashes are deterministic; core starts offline without optional imports; each feature is exercised only in its declared environment and is unavailable until a compatible payload is atomically enabled.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep the prior compatible capability reference, quarantine the failed staging, and leave the feature unavailable with actionable diagnostics.

tasks.subject: Implement platform browser selection and readiness
tasks.observableResult: Windows selects system Edge, then system Chrome, then managed Chromium; macOS selects system Chrome, then managed Chromium; Safari appears only as an explicit experimental safaridriver adapter with a truthful warning and no Playwright promise.
tasks.expectedResult: Command exits 0 for simulated platform matrices; supported choices pass the local fake; experimental/unsupported paths explain limitations; fallback never contacts the real service.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Fall back only in documented order, retain the prior compatible managed browser, and leave acquisition unavailable when readiness or a non-capability error fails.

tasks.subject: Assemble and validate the immutable release channel
tasks.observableResult: Native core/capability artifacts become one immutable, hash-bound, provider-neutral release channel that supports first install, update, resume, and offline restart through a local fake before an approval-gated publication step.
commands: uv run pytest tests/release/test_release_channel.py tests/release/test_update_policy.py tests/integration/test_release_server.py tests/ci/test_release_workflow.py -q
uv run python tools/assemble_release_channel.py --artifacts build/native-artifacts --capabilities build/capabilities --output build/release-channel
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0; local fake flows pass with no external request; channel validation rejects mutable names, missing/incompatible metadata, escaping paths, size/hash mismatch, stale update state, and undeclared payloads; publication cannot run without the release environment approval.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Block publication, retain the last valid immutable channel, quarantine only the failed candidate, and rebuild all affected manifests/evidence from the exact lock.

tasks.subject: Build and verify native sub-18 MB Windows and macOS installers
tasks.observableResult: A native Windows 11 x64 runner and native macOS 14+ arm64 runner each produce a thin installer at most 18 MB that installs core without system Python, can add capabilities, and restarts offline; unchanged Windows 10 x64 results remain best effort.
commands: uv run python tools/build_installers.py --platform windows-x86_64 --output build/native/windows-x86_64
uv run python tools/build_installers.py --platform macos-arm64 --output build/native/macos-arm64
uv run python tools/collect_native_artifacts.py --input build/native --output dist/installers
uv run pytest tests/release/test_installer_budget.py tests/release/test_platform_contract.py tests/ci/test_release_workflow.py -q
uv run python tools/rehearse_clean_install.py --artifact-dir build/native/windows-x86_64 --release-channel build/release-channel --without-system-python --offline-restart
uv run python tools/rehearse_clean_install.py --artifact-dir build/native/macos-arm64 --release-channel build/release-channel --without-system-python --offline-restart
tasks.expectedResult: Every native and aggregation command exits 0; each installer is at most 18 MB; clean first launch downloads only core from the fake channel; optional payloads remain separate; egress- denied restart succeeds; Windows 10 failure is recorded without blocking supported targets.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Do not publish an oversized, cross-built, or failed artifact. Remove only operation- owned staging, retain last-known-good installers, and reduce launcher closure rather than raising the budget.

tasks.subject: Add redacted diagnostics and future telemetry protocols
tasks.observableResult: Structured rotating logs, sanitized support bundles, versioned allowlisted event DTOs, ObservabilityPort, NoopObservability, and TelemetrySpool protocol operate with no telemetry dependency, durable spool, or network exporter in the shipped product.
commands: uv run pytest tests/observability tests/packaging/test_core_imports.py tests/privacy/test_diagnostics.py -q
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0; the default creates no telemetry record or network request; OpenTelemetry packages are absent from core; fake protocol tests pass; support bundles retain only allowlisted redacted diagnostics.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep NoopObservability selected, reject invalid event DTOs, and regenerate only the user-requested support bundle. Do not introduce a local spool as a repair.

tasks.subject: Produce exact release supply-chain evidence
tasks.observableResult: Vulnerability results, approved licenses, per-payload CycloneDX SBOMs, archive/secret scans, artifact hashes, authoritative version, source revision, capability manifests, and native clean-build metadata form one reproducible release evidence bundle.
commands: uv run python tools/build_release_evidence.py --channel build/release-channel --installers dist/installers --capabilities build/capabilities --output build/evidence/release
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0; evidence references every exact artifact hash, lock digest, build-tool version, git revision, license, and SBOM; no unreviewed finding remains; signing is deferred-internal.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Block publication, keep the last clean evidence bundle, update/remove the affected dependency or artifact, rebuild natively from the lock, and regenerate the entire bundle.

tasks.subject: Lock measured resource and performance limits
tasks.observableResult: Release configuration contains measured non-placeholder limits for uploads, PDF pages/image dimensions, parse time/memory, archives, jobs/workers, queue depth, shutdown grace, cache/disk reserve, startup, request counts, runtime, installer size, and installed footprint.
commands: uv run python tools/measure_baseline.py --corpus synthetic --repetitions 5 --machine-class controlled --compare build/baseline.json --output build/release-baseline.json
tasks.expectedResult: Commands exit 0 on the controlled runner; every limit records value, unit, measurement, machine class, variance, threshold, headroom rationale, safe range, and failure behavior; no hard or tolerant regression exceeds policy.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Keep prior measured limits, reject the candidate, profile the regressed path, and rerun on the same machine class. Do not widen limits without new evidence and review.

tasks.subject: Final acceptance, documentation, and legacy retirement
tasks.observableResult: All three gate records and D1-D7 are green; current documentation lets an operator install, update, recover, migrate, manage/delete retained data, run offline, add/remove capabilities, create redacted diagnostics, and invoke the explicit staging smoke; redundant legacy implementation is removed while compatibility entry points remain for the transition window.
commands: uv run python tools/verify_release.py --channel build/release-channel --evidence build/evidence/release --installers dist/installers --capabilities build/capabilities
tasks.expectedResult: Every command exits 0; branch/package thresholds meet policy; wheel, sdist, channel, native installers, capabilities, and evidence verify; all offline flows work; no stale implementation, sensitive artifact, unexpected skip, network escape, placeholder limit, or unresolved decision remains.
tasks.recoveryBehavior: Do not publish or migrate the live installation. Restore the last-known-good release bundle, return the failure to its owning task, and rerun D8 in full after repair.
